items.goal: Invalid cancel/ship status transitions on PUT /api/orders/cancel and /api/orders/ship return 409 (rule violation) or 404 (order not found) instead of 500.

subject: implementer
reason: The cancel/ship 409/400/404 mapping in OrdersApi is correct, but rethrowing OrderingDomainException in the shared IdentifiedCommandHandler base changes CreateOrder and every integration-event handler: CreateOrder now escapes as an unhandled 500 and event consumers now see exceptions they never did. Root cause: a cross-cutting base class was changed for two endpoints.

items.reason: The catch/rethrow of OrderingDomainException applies to every IdentifiedCommandHandler subclass. CreateOrderAsync (OrdersApi.cs:201) has no try/catch, so a rule or validation failure on create order now becomes an unhandled exception instead of the previous handled outcome. SetPaid, SetStockConfirmed, SetStockRejected and SetAwaitingValidation event handlers now throw to the event bus on invalid transitions instead of being swallowed.
items.fix: Scope the rethrow to cancel and ship only (a virtual hook or flag on those handlers), or keep the swallow in the base class and surface rule violations another way. Keep CreateOrder and the event handlers' behaviour unchanged, or handle the exception in CreateOrderAsync explicitly.

items.reason: CreateRequestForCommandAsync persists the request id before the command runs. After a rejected cancel or ship (409/400) the id stays stored, and a retry with the same x-requestid returns 200 through the duplicate-request path, a false success for an operation that failed.
items.fix: Record the request id only after the command succeeds, or remove or roll it back when OrderingDomainException is thrown or the command returns false.
